observations: The original maintained verifier accepts the same valid TOTP value on a second password challenge, returning 200 and leaving two sessions. The exact original-product regression fails three assertions.

The existing native factor row now retains bounded fingerprints of already verified codes. A database constraint bounds the array to 16 entries; successful use drops expired entries. Neither plaintext codes nor another identity/factor system is stored.

The 90-second database-time consumption window covers the maintained verifier's current and adjacent 30-second steps. Fingerprints remain on the same factor across password and backup-code changes and disappear with the factor on erasure. Retained bounded fingerprints are security metadata, not a timed physical-erasure claim.

The first atomic implementation passes 46 cases but rolls consumption back when later session creation fails. A new actual native session-write failure regression demonstrates code reuse after that rollback; the exact stage is archived.

Final consumption commits in an independent proof-pinned transaction after real provider verification. Session publication repeats current user/factor checks, uses the original verification time and cannot restore the consumed value on failure.

The current native session is physically pinned during in-session TOTP completion using the shared proof owner. A separate PostgreSQL transaction cannot acquire a conflicting lock while the real native replacement is being created.

Two actual concurrent password challenges using one new valid code yield one successful completion. Reuse after a password change and after injected native session-write failure is refused. All real verifiers remain maintained provider code. Tests use the provider's maintained current/adjacent-step generators without changing clocks.

Final four complete PostgreSQL/HTTP suites pass 48 cases; final server compiler and native migration checks return zero. Native generation creates 0523 and prunes only the oldest snapshot; no committed migration SQL is edited.
